choosing-integration-methods-s2.title: A student's work on <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mn>0</mn><mn>1</mn></msubsup><mfrac><mrow><mn>6</mn><mi>x</mi></mrow><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mfrac><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\int_0^1 \frac{6x}{x^2 + 1}\,dx</annotation></semantics></math>
choosing-integration-methods-s2.html:

StepWork

items.q: Which is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>3</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{x^2 + 3x + 5}{x + 1}</annotation></semantics></math> after long division?

Find <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mfrac><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>3</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mfrac><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\int \frac{x^2 + 3x + 5}{x + 1}\,dx</annotation></semantics></math> for <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>></mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x > -1</annotation></semantics></math>. Include <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">+</mo><mi>C</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+ C</annotation></semantics></math>.

mistakes.why: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mfrac><mn>3</mn><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mfrac><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\int \frac{3}{x + 1}\,dx</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mn>3</mn><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= 3\ln|x + 1|</annotation></semantics></math>; the inside is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x + 1</annotation></semantics></math>, not <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math>.

The top and the bottom cannot be integrated separately. Divide first: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>+</mo><mfrac><mn>3</mn><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x + 2 + \frac{3}{x + 1}</annotation></semantics></math>.

The remainder term <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>3</mn><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{3}{x + 1}</annotation></semantics></math> is missing; it integrates to <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>3</mn><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3\ln|x + 1|</annotation></semantics></math>.

expr.answerHtml: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>3</mn><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">|</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">|</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>+</mo><mi>C</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{x^{2}}{2} + 2x + 3\,\ln(\left|x + 1\right|) + C</annotation></semantics></math>

items.q: Using the division above, evaluate the definite integral <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mn>0</mn><mn>2</mn></msubsup><mfrac><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>3</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mfrac><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\int_0^2 \frac{x^2 + 3x + 5}{x + 1}\,dx</annotation></semantics></math>.

mistakes.why: The remainder term contributes <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>3</mn><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><msubsup><mo stretchy="true" symmetric="true" minsize="1.8em" maxsize="1.8em">|</mo><mn>0</mn><mn>2</mn></msubsup><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3\ln|x + 1|\Big|_0^2 = 3\ln 3</annotation></semantics></math>.

At <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = 2</annotation></semantics></math>, <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x + 1 = 3</annotation></semantics></math>: the log term is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>3</mn><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>3</mn><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3\ln 3 - 3\ln 1 = 3\ln 3</annotation></semantics></math>.

numeric.answerHtml: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>6</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>3</mn><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">6 + 3\,\ln(3)</annotation></semantics></math>

items.q: Why is long division the right first step for this integrand?
options: The top and bottom can each be integrated on their own
The top's degree, 2, is at least the bottom's, 1
The top is the derivative of the bottom
The bottom has no real zeros, so arctan applies

items.q: Complete the square in the denominator: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>10</mn><mo>=</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x^2 - 2x + 10 =</annotation></semantics></math>

Find <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>10</mn></mrow></mfrac><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\int \frac{1}{x^2 - 2x + 10}\,dx</annotation></semantics></math>. Include <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">+</mo><mi>C</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+ C</annotation></semantics></math>.

mistakes.why: With <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>u</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mn>3</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">u = \frac{x - 1}{3}</annotation></semantics></math>, <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>u</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">dx = 3\,du</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>9</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>9</mn><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>u</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(x - 1)^2 + 9 = 9(u^2 + 1)</annotation></semantics></math>: the result has a factor <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>3</mn><mn>9</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>3</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{3}{9} = \frac{1}{3}</annotation></semantics></math>.

That would fit <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{(x - 1)^2 + 1}</annotation></semantics></math>. Here the constant is 9, so scale by 3: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>3</mn></mfrac><mi>arctan</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">(</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mn>3</mn></mfrac><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{3}\arctan\left(\frac{x - 1}{3}\right)</annotation></semantics></math>.

The <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ln</annotation></semantics></math> form needs the derivative of the bottom, <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2x - 2</annotation></semantics></math>, on top. With 1 on top, complete the square and use arctan.

items.q: Find <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mn>1</mn><mn>4</mn></msubsup><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>10</mn></mrow></mfrac><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\int_1^4 \frac{1}{x^2 - 2x + 10}\,dx</annotation></semantics></math>.

mistakes.why: That is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>arctan</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>arctan</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\arctan 1 - \arctan 0</annotation></semantics></math> without the factor <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>3</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{3}</annotation></semantics></math>.

At <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = 4</annotation></semantics></math>, <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mn>3</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{x - 1}{3} = 1</annotation></semantics></math>, not 3: substitute into <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mn>3</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{x - 1}{3}</annotation></semantics></math>.

items.q: Why does this integrand lead to arctan rather than to a logarithm?
options: Any fraction with a quadratic on the bottom gives arctan
The bottom has no real zeros and the top is a constant
The top is the derivative of the bottom
The degree of the top is at least the degree of the bottom

items.q: Write the top as <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(x^2 + 1) - 1</annotation></semantics></math>, then antidifferentiate <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mfrac><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mfrac><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\int \frac{x^2}{x^2 + 1}\,dx</annotation></semantics></math>. Include <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">+</mo><mi>C</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+ C</annotation></semantics></math>.

mistakes.why: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mfrac><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\int \frac{1}{x^2 + 1}\,dx</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mi>arctan</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \arctan x</annotation></semantics></math>; the <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ln</annotation></semantics></math> form needs <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2x</annotation></semantics></math> on top.

<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{x^2}{x^2 + 1}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= 1 - \frac{1}{x^2 + 1}</annotation></semantics></math>: the arctan term is subtracted.

items.q: Split off the quotient, then antidifferentiate <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mfrac><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\int \frac{2x + 3}{x + 1}\,dx</annotation></semantics></math> for <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>></mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x > -1</annotation></semantics></math>. Include <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">+</mo><mi>C</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+ C</annotation></semantics></math>.

mistakes.why: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2x + 3 = 2(x + 1) + 1</annotation></semantics></math>: the remainder is 1, not 3.
Integrate after dividing, not the top and bottom separately.

expr.answerHtml: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">|</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">|</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>+</mo><mi>C</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2x + \ln(\left|x + 1\right|) + C</annotation></semantics></math>

items.q: Find <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>4</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow></mfrac><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\int \frac{1}{x^2 + 4x + 5}\,dx</annotation></semantics></math>. Include <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">+</mo><mi>C</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+ C</annotation></semantics></math>.

mistakes.why: Half of 4 is 2: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>4</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x^2 + 4x + 5</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= (x + 2)^2 + 1</annotation></semantics></math>.

The top would have to be <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2x + 4</annotation></semantics></math> for the <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ln</annotation></semantics></math> form. With 1 on top, complete the square.

items.q: Find <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>9</mn></mrow></mfrac><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\int \frac{1}{x^2 + 9}\,dx</annotation></semantics></math>. Include <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">+</mo><mi>C</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+ C</annotation></semantics></math>.

mistakes.why: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>9</mn></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{x^2 + 9}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>9</mn></mfrac><mo>⋅</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>/</mo><mn>3</mn><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \frac{1}{9}\cdot\frac{1}{(x/3)^2 + 1}</annotation></semantics></math>; with <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>u</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mi>x</mi><mn>3</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">u = \frac{x}{3}</annotation></semantics></math>, <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>u</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">dx = 3\,du</annotation></semantics></math>, which leaves <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>3</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{3}</annotation></semantics></math>.

The <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>9</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{9}</annotation></semantics></math> is offset by <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>u</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">dx = 3\,du</annotation></semantics></math>: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>3</mn><mn>9</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>3</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{3}{9} = \frac{1}{3}</annotation></semantics></math>.

items.q: Which integral is best started by completing the square?

Divide the top by <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x^2 + 1</annotation></semantics></math> first, then evaluate <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mn>0</mn><mn>1</mn></msubsup><mfrac><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mfrac><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\int_0^1 \frac{x^3 + x + 1}{x^2 + 1}\,dx</annotation></semantics></math>.

mistakes.why: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mn>0</mn><mn>1</mn></msubsup><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mfrac><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\int_0^1 \frac{1}{x^2 + 1}\,dx</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mi>arctan</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \arctan 1</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>4</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \frac{\pi}{4}</annotation></semantics></math>. The <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ln</annotation></semantics></math> form needs <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2x</annotation></semantics></math> on top.

The remainder term <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{x^2 + 1}</annotation></semantics></math> adds <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>4</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{\pi}{4}</annotation></semantics></math>.

items.q: Find <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mfrac><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mfrac><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\int \frac{x^3 - 1}{x - 1}\,dx</annotation></semantics></math> for <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>≠</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x \ne 1</annotation></semantics></math>.

Find <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>8</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>20</mn></mrow></mfrac><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\int \frac{1}{x^2 + 8x + 20}\,dx</annotation></semantics></math>.

Which integral is set up for the substitution <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>u</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">u = x^2</annotation></semantics></math>?
Which integral should start with polynomial long division?

Evaluate integral III, <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></mfrac><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\int \frac{1}{x^2 + 2x + 2}\,dx</annotation></semantics></math>. Include <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">+</mo><mi>C</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+ C</annotation></semantics></math>.

mistakes.why: The <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ln</annotation></semantics></math> form needs the bottom's derivative, <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2x + 2</annotation></semantics></math>, on top. With 1 on top, complete the square: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(x + 1)^2 + 1</annotation></semantics></math>.

Half of 2 is 1: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x^2 + 2x + 2</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= (x + 1)^2 + 1</annotation></semantics></math>.

items.q: Evaluate integral IV, <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mfrac><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mfrac><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\int \frac{x^2 + 1}{x - 1}\,dx</annotation></semantics></math> for <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>></mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x > 1</annotation></semantics></math>. Include <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">+</mo><mi>C</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+ C</annotation></semantics></math>.

mistakes.why: The remainder is 2: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(x - 1)(x + 1) = x^2 - 1</annotation></semantics></math>, and <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x^2 + 1 - (x^2 - 1) = 2</annotation></semantics></math>.

The quotient is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x + 1</annotation></semantics></math>: check by multiplying, <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(x - 1)(x + 1) + 2</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= x^2 + 1</annotation></semantics></math>.

expr.answerHtml: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>+</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">|</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">|</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>+</mo><mi>C</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{x^{2}}{2} + x + 2\,\ln(\left|x - 1\right|) + C</annotation></semantics></math>

items.q: Where is the first error in the student work?
options: Step 2: the limits 0 and 1 were not changed to values of u
Step 2: the factor should be 6, not 3

Step 3: the antiderivative of <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mi>u</mi></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{u}</annotation></semantics></math> is not <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mi>u</mi><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ln|u|</annotation></semantics></math>

items.q: Find the correct value of <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mn>0</mn><mn>1</mn></msubsup><mfrac><mrow><mn>6</mn><mi>x</mi></mrow><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mfrac><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\int_0^1 \frac{6x}{x^2 + 1}\,dx</annotation></semantics></math>.

mistakes.why: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>6</mn><mi>x</mi><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>u</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">6x\,dx = 3\,du</annotation></semantics></math>; the factor is 3, not 6.

The arctan form is for a constant on top. Here the top is a multiple of the bottom's derivative: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ln</annotation></semantics></math>.

items.q: Which check confirms that <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>3</mn><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3\ln(x^2 + 1)</annotation></semantics></math> is an antiderivative of <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mn>6</mn><mi>x</mi></mrow><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{6x}{x^2 + 1}</annotation></semantics></math>?
options: Its graph looks like a parabola near 0

items.q: Another student writes <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>6</mn><mi>x</mi></mrow><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mfrac><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\int \frac{6x}{x^2 + 1}\,dx</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mn>6</mn><mi>arctan</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>C</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= 6\arctan x + C</annotation></semantics></math>. What is the reason this is wrong?
options: The answer should have <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">+</mo><mn>6</mn><mi>C</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+ 6C</annotation></semantics></math>

The <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math> in the numerator: arctan fits <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{x^2 + 1}</annotation></semantics></math>, not <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mi>x</mi><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{x}{x^2 + 1}</annotation></semantics></math>

Arctan needs <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msqrt><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></msqrt></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sqrt{1 - x^2}</annotation></semantics></math> on the bottom

items.q: Find <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>4</mn><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></mfrac><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\int \frac{1}{1 + 4x^2}\,dx</annotation></semantics></math>.

Find <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><msup><mi>sec</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>3</mn><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\int \sec^2(3x)\,dx</annotation></semantics></math>. Include <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">+</mo><mi>C</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+ C</annotation></semantics></math>.

mistakes.why: Its derivative is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>3</mn><msup><mi>sec</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>3</mn><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3\sec^2(3x)</annotation></semantics></math>. Divide by the 3 from the inside.

The power rule does not apply to <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>sec</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sec^2</annotation></semantics></math>; read <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mi>d</mi><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow></mfrac><mi>tan</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>u</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>sec</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>u</mi><mo>⋅</mo><mrow><mi>u</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{d}{dx}\tan u = \sec^2 u \cdot u'</annotation></semantics></math> backward.

expr.lhsHtml: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><msup><mi>sec</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>3</mn><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\int \sec^2(3x)\,dx =</annotation></semantics></math>

items.q: Find <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><msqrt><mi>x</mi></msqrt></mfrac><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\int \frac{x + 1}{\sqrt{x}}\,dx</annotation></semantics></math> for <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>></mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x > 0</annotation></semantics></math>. Include <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">+</mo><mi>C</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+ C</annotation></semantics></math>.

mistakes.why: The top and the bottom cannot be integrated separately. Split first: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>+</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x^{1/2} + x^{-1/2}</annotation></semantics></math>.

<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\int x^{-1/2}\,dx</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mfrac><msup><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \frac{x^{1/2}}{1/2}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mn>2</mn><msup><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= 2x^{1/2}</annotation></semantics></math>: the power goes up to <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{2}</annotation></semantics></math>.

items.q: Find <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mi>x</mi><msqrt><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msqrt><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\int x\sqrt{x - 1}\,dx</annotation></semantics></math> for <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>></mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x > 1</annotation></semantics></math>, using <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>u</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">u = x - 1</annotation></semantics></math>. Include <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">+</mo><mi>C</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+ C</annotation></semantics></math>.

mistakes.why: The <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math> outside cannot be treated as a constant. With <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>u</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">u = x - 1</annotation></semantics></math>, write <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>u</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = u + 1</annotation></semantics></math>: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>u</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><msup><mi>u</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>u</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\int (u + 1)u^{1/2}\,du</annotation></semantics></math>.

An integral of a product is not the product of the integrals. Rewrite <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>u</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = u + 1</annotation></semantics></math> and expand.

items.q: Pick a method and evaluate <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mn>0</mn><mrow><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msubsup><mfrac><msup><mi>e</mi><mi>x</mi></msup><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><msup><mi>e</mi><mi>x</mi></msup></mrow></mfrac><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\int_0^{\ln 2} \frac{e^x}{1 + e^x}\,dx</annotation></semantics></math>.

mistakes.why: At <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = 0</annotation></semantics></math>, <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><msup><mi>e</mi><mn>0</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1 + e^0 = 2</annotation></semantics></math>, so subtract <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ln 2</annotation></semantics></math>: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ln 3 - \ln 2</annotation></semantics></math>.

That evaluates the integrand-like expression <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><msup><mi>e</mi><mi>x</mi></msup></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{1 + e^x}</annotation></semantics></math>. With <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>u</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><msup><mi>e</mi><mi>x</mi></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">u = 1 + e^x</annotation></semantics></math> the antiderivative is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mi>u</mi><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ln|u|</annotation></semantics></math>.

items.q: Find <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><mrow><msup><mi>sin</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow></mfrac><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\int \frac{\cos x}{\sin^2 x}\,dx</annotation></semantics></math>.
options: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>sin</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>+</mo><mi>C</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ln(\sin^2 x) + C</annotation></semantics></math>

<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo>+</mo><mi>C</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{\sin x}{-\cos x} + C</annotation></semantics></math>

<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo>+</mo><mi>C</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-\frac{1}{\sin x} + C</annotation></semantics></math>

items.q: Choose a substitution and evaluate <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mn>1</mn><mi>e</mi></msubsup><mfrac><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><mi>x</mi></mfrac><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\int_1^{e} \frac{1 + \ln x}{x}\,dx</annotation></semantics></math>.

mistakes.why: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></msubsup><mi>u</mi><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>u</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\int_1^2 u\,du</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mfrac><msup><mi>u</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mn>2</mn></mfrac><msubsup><mo stretchy="true" symmetric="true" minsize="1.8em" maxsize="1.8em">|</mo><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></msubsup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \frac{u^2}{2}\Big|_1^2</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>4</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \frac{4 - 1}{2}</annotation></semantics></math>: keep the <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{2}</annotation></semantics></math>.

With <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>u</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">u = 1 + \ln x</annotation></semantics></math>, the limits are 1 and 2, not 0 and 2: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>4</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>−</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{4}{2} - \frac{1}{2}</annotation></semantics></math>.

items.q: Which of these has no antiderivative that can be written with the functions of this course, so a definite integral of it is found with a calculator?
